title: Equinox POC - Security Evidence Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures our responses to Equinox's security questionnaire, maps required artifacts to owners, and records workshop notes and next steps for the Dedicated/Private POC. Intended as a single-source checklist to assemble the audit packet for the customer and their internal auditors.

Scope:
- Equinox is evaluating Redwood Dedicated with optional Private VPC + HSM integration for regulated financial workflows.
- Deliverables: completed questionnaire (.xlsx), evidence bundle (logs, configs, screenshots, scripts), demo recordings, and a short security briefing doc for their auditors.

Quick summary answers (high level):
- Data residency: Customer can run in their VPC / region; default hosted plane not used in Private deployment.
- Encryption: TLS1.2+ for in-transit; AES-256 for data-at-rest; customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM supported.
- Access control: SAML SSO + RBAC; service accounts with scoped tokens; audit logging for admin actions.
- Isolation: Dedicated GPU pools + network segmentation (VPC subnets and NSGs).

Evidence inventory (what we will provide):
1) Architecture diagrams:
   - network-segmentation-diagram.puml (owner: Marco Diaz)
   - private-control-plane-deployment.yaml (rendered topology, owner: Marco Diaz)
2) Identity & access:
   - saml-assertion-example.txt (sensitive redacted, owner: Priya Singh)
   - rbac-role-matrix.csv (owner: Priya Singh)
3) Cryptography / keys:
   - hsm-integration-runbook.md (owner: Aisha Patel)
   - kms-key-rotation-policy.pdf (sample policy template, owner: Security Ops)
   - keywrap-demo-recording.mp4 (redacted, owner: Aisha Patel)
4) Logging & monitoring:
   - audit-log-retention-policy.md (owner: SRE)
   - example-admin-audit-log-2026-02-21.ndjson (sample records, redacted, owner: Jonah Kim)
   - prometheus-slo-dashboard-export.json (owner: Observability)
5) Operational controls:
   - incident-response-runbook.pdf (owner: SRE)
   - deployment-rollback-playbook.txt (owner: Release Eng)
6) Hardening & patching:
   - image-build-checklist.txt (owner: Infra)
   - monthly-patch-report-2026-01.pdf (owner: Platform Eng)
7) Pen test / vuln scan:
   - vuln-scan-summary-2025-12.csv (owner: Security)

Control mapping notes (working):
- SOC 2 / ISO mapping: We will mark each artifact with which control it supports. Quick draft mapping attached in Jira-1234.
- For HSM questions, provide: HSM vendor attestation, key usage policy, and demo of sign/unwrap flow.

Outstanding questionnaire items (customer asked for clarifications):
- Q: Can Redwood guarantee that KV caches are never written to disk?
  A: Runtime is configured to keep KV cache in ephemeral device memory; we will provide config snippets and a short demo showing filesystem mounts. Owner: Marco.
- Q: What is the SLA for key rotation if customer uses Redwood KMS?
  A: We provide recommended rotation cadence and automation hooks; for customer-managed KMS/HSM we will point to their rotation policy. Owner: Aisha.
- Q: Can we demonstrate separation between control plane and data plane?
  A: Yes — schedule deep-dive with infra (diagram + demo). Owner: Marco/Priya.

Workshop notes (2026-02-20 session with Equinox security + platform):
- Attendees: Equinox (Lead Sec: Erica Nolan), Redwood (Aisha, Marco, Priya, Jonah).
- Main concerns: HSM key escrow, audit log tamper-proofing, data exfil risk from model outputs.
- Action items captured live:
   * Provide HSM keywrap demo (Aisha) — due 2026-02-27.
   * Prepare sample audit-log export with WORM-like retention options (Jonah) — due 2026-03-03.
   * Clarify encryption-at-rest for ephemeral NVMe caches (Marco) — due 2026-02-25.
   * Draft customer-facing security brief summarizing controls (Priya) — due 2026-02-28.
- Notes-to-self: Equinox wants explicit examples of fallback model variants; highlight that fallbacks do not exchange plaintext customer data with other tenants.

Risk / gaps we should call out to customer (transparency):
- Currently we have an ongoing work item to formalize our cross-region key management for private deployments; timeline 2026-Q2.
- Some low-level runtime hardening documents are internal only; we will extract redacted excerpts and create a customer-friendly artifact.

Packaging plan / delivery format:
- Create a single zip: equinox-security-packet-2026-03.zip containing:
   * questionnaire-completed.xlsx
   * evidence/ (folder with artifacts above)
   * recording-links.txt (hosted in secure S3 with expiring links)
   * readme.txt with catalog and control mapping
- Delivery method: shared secure link (pre-signed S3) + brief walkthrough call with Equinox audit team.

Suggested reviewer checklist before handoff:
- All artifacts redacted for PII/credentials.
- Owner sign-off for each file (Slack confirmation is fine).
- Confirm pre-signed links expire in <=7 days.
- Attach conformance mapping (which artifact maps to which SOC2/ISO control) in the readme.

Appendix - sample redaction notes (working):
- Replace tenant IDs with <TENANT_ID> token.
- Remove any full user email addresses; use role@equivalent.example.
- In logs, keep timestamps and action types; redact longstack traces that include GUIDs.

Raw workshop transcript fragments (copied during meeting):
- "We need a real example where a key is rotated during active sessions — what happens to cached KV?" — Erica
- "Runtime supports hot-rotate of keys; cached KV stays encrypted with previous wrapping until cache TTL or explicit rewrap is invoked." — Aisha
- "Can we get a timeline for private control plane onboarding?" — Equinox eng lead

Next steps (short term):
1) Deliver HSM demo recording and runbook (Aisha)
2) Produce redacted audit log sample (Jonah)
3) Complete questionnaire workbook and annotate answers with artifact links (Priya)
4) Internal review with Security & SRE for sign-off (target 2026-03-05)

Notes / comments (scratch):
- Might ask legal to provide a short mutual NDA addendum for deeper evidence sharing.
- Consider offering a short in-person lab for their auditors if remote evidence insufficient.

End of playbook (working).

-- Aisha Patel (solutions engineering)
